You may not be able to have a pet otter, but depending on where you live, you can have a pet fox.
We have wild foxes around where I live. I've only seen one once but I'm told that once in a while you will see one roaming our parking lot at night. Foxes are beautiful, I'd be down with a pet fox.

I've done serious research about owning pet foxes. You have to be up for some serious commitment. They'll require a secure place to run around and dig, you'll need to train them to hunt in case they manage to escape, you'll need to find a vet who can give foxes proper medical care, they have a very specific diet (can't just feed your fox regular doggy kibble), they're high energy, high maintenance, have a certain scent to them (like ferrets) and aren't completely domesticated like dogs and cats are.

On the flip side, they're super fun, very playful, loyal, affectionate, can get along great with other animals and are pretty intelligent. If you're serious about adopting a fox, then spend a lot of time researching them. You'll probably want to go with a fennec fox if you're in the US (less likely to get in trouble with a fennec), so check out Scout the fennec fox on YouTube to watch how he behaves. Find someone with a pet fox (if you can) and spend time playing/caring for the fox if they let you. And also look into fox/exotic animal sanctuaries within a few hundred miles of where you live in case you need to give up the fennec for whatever reason because your typical animal shelter won't take in stray exotics.

Sorry for the essay, but if you're serious about wanting to own a fox, you really need to do your homework. They're awesome and badass pets, but they require a lot of time and energy.
